newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee climbs to contract highs as specs buy.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee climbs to contract highs as specs buy.

text.p: Nearby CSCE coffee futures punched higher ahead of midday as brisk speculative buying pushed active July to new life-of-contract high of 250.50 cents a lb, dealers said.
At 1146 EDT, July stood at 248.75 cents, up 8.15 cents, after sinking to a low of 238.00 this morning. Spot May rose 7.50 to 269.00, while the back months rose 3.00 to 7.50.

Coffee prices gapped higher at the outset after locals came in to cover short positions, traders said. A bout of profit taking pushed the market briefly into negative territory, but speculators -- led by commission houses -- started buying.

Some traders said the buying was inspired by long-term weather outlooks calling for a cool airmass to make its way from Argentina into Brazil. But forecasters warned the chance of damaging frost was slim.

"It is going to turn much colder in Argentina next week," said Weather Services Corp. meterologist Mike Palmerino. "Some of cool air could spill into Brazil, but its a far cry from having a freeze in Brazil's coffee areas."
